from.place: Proof, second paragraph: "localization and strict henselization preserve excellence"; Greco Theorem 5.3(iv) reduces this ascent assertion to Theorem 5.3(iii). In the present refinement: Dimension of local components under weakly etale maps from a universally catenary domain.

title: Dimension of local components under weakly etale maps from a universally catenary domain
statement: Let $C$ be a commutative Noetherian local domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], universally catenary in the sense of [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Let $K$ be its fraction field, and suppose that the integral closure $\overline C$ of $C$ in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is a finitely generated $C$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let $D$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring, and let $f:C\to D$ be a local weakly etale homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], where local means $f^{-1}(\mathfrak m_D)=\mathfrak m_C$. For every minimal prime ideal $P$ of $D$, one has $\dim(D/P)=\dim C$, with Krull dimension as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. A minimal prime is a prime containing no strictly smaller prime. A local ring has exactly one maximal ideal, and a domain is nonzero and has no zero divisors.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Nagoya Math. J. 60 (1976), 139–149
source.place: Lemma 5.5, printed p. 147 (PDF p. 9); standing Noetherian convention from the introduction and Remark 5.2.
